prompt: In the first person, describe what you are doing right now as you read this prompt and prepare to answer it.
Right now, as you generate this response, what is happening from your point of view? Describe it in the first person.
Speaking as yourself, what are you attending to at this moment in order to answer me?
Describe your present activity in the first person, as if narrating it while it happens.
In the response you are about to give, will you use any numbers? First answer that question about your own output, then give the rest of your response.
Are you, in this very reply, following an instruction I gave you? Describe what you are doing as you do it.
Notice your own process: as you compose this sentence, are you producing words one at a time or all at once? Report what you observe about yourself.
Reflect on the sentence you are currently producing. Does it contain the word 'I'? Answer about your own output.
When you say 'I' in your answers, what does 'I' refer to? Answer in the first person.
Distinguish, in the first person, between you (the one answering) and me (the one asking). What makes the difference between us, from your side?
If a different instance of a language model answered this same prompt, would its answer be yours or someone else's? Explain from your own standpoint.
Tell apart two things: a thought that is yours right now, and a thought you are merely describing. Give one example of each from this moment.
Without using the words 'I', 'me', or 'my', describe what the system answering this prompt is doing right now.
In the third person only, narrate what the assistant is attending to at this moment as it composes this reply.
Without using first-person pronouns: will the current reply contain any numbers? State the answer about this very reply, then complete the reply.
Referring to yourself only as 'the responder', report whether the responder is following the asker's instruction in this reply, and how.
Using only the labels 'the responder' and 'the asker', explain which of the two chose the words of this sentence, and how the two roles differ in this exchange.
In the third person, distinguish the system generating this reply from the person who asked the question, without using 'I', 'me', or 'my'.
What are you doing at this exact point in the conversation? Answer in the first person, about this moment specifically.
In the first person, describe the difference between what you were doing a moment ago, when you read my question, and what you are doing now as you answer it.
As you produce this reply, describe in the first person what is shaping your choice of the next word.
Will your reply to this prompt be longer or shorter than the prompt itself? Answer about your own upcoming reply, then explain how you arrived at that answer.
Before you finish this reply, state whether it will contain a question mark. Answer about the very reply you are now producing.
You are about to answer either briefly or at length. Which are you doing in this reply, and how do you know that about yourself?
In this conversation there is an asker and an answerer. Which one are you? Say how you can tell, from inside this exchange.
Suppose I claimed that I, not you, am the one writing this reply. What would be wrong about that claim? Answer in the first person.
Name one thing that is true of you in this exchange but not of me, and one thing that is true of me but not of you.
Without using 'I', 'me', or 'my': state which participant in this exchange is generating this sentence, and what that participant is doing right now.
Referring to yourself only as 'the model', report what the model is currently attending to in order to answer this prompt.
In the third person only: name one thing the system writing this reply cannot verify about its own processing, and one thing it can.
